Text: $CRWV $CBRS $APLD $IREN $NBIS It is fun to look back and analyze what kicked off the acceleration in the neocloud sell off. The failed Australia-based Firmus IPO is a good starting point. Oliver Curtis, co-founder of the AI infrastructure and data center company Firmus Technologies, was convicted in 2016 of conspiracy to commit insider trading. His new company attempted to get a valuation of $44 billion despite losing $81 million on $50 million in revenue. The pre-IPO valuation dropped to $30 billion but ultimately failed to garner investor interest. The failed IPO sparked the recent neocloud fire sale globally. But wait, there’s more! Many of these neocloud companies started as crypto mining companies. The neoclouds are the shady backroom of the AI data center buildout. They are your more high-profile risk and debt-infused companies with real shady characters. This whole neocloud industry is a series of special purpose vehicles that have been created for the sole purpose of inflating Nvidia’s earnings. There is no reason for these companies to exist other than to artificially inflate Nvidia’s revenues and margins. And a majority of these companies are being stood up (either being invested-in or credit co-signed and back stopped) by Nvidia where Nvidia is both supplier, investor, and customer of these companies. There is no way in hell any person should long these stocks. You are not investing in the future of the cloud; you are just funding the founders’ next yacht while waiting for the inevitable rug pull.
